title: ClaimArbitrage internal swaps use no slippage protection, enabling sandwich attacks
description: All conversion swaps use type(uint160).min+1 or type(uint160).max-1 as sqrtPriceLimitX96 -- effectively zero slippage protection. While the pump/unwind swaps have pumpPriceLimit/unwindPriceLimit, the stablecoin conversion and profit conversion swaps have no bounds.
impact: MEV bots can sandwich the execute() transaction, manipulating pool prices before execution. The NoProfit check prevents total loss but the sandwich extracts value from the profitable margin. Reduces effective discount rate for legitimate arbitrageurs.
attackPath: Front-run: manipulate prices in the stable->USDC and/or USDC->WETH pools
ClaimArbitrage.execute() swaps at manipulated prices with no slippage bounds
Back-run: unwind the price manipulation for profit
Value extracted from ClaimArbitrage's profit margin; NoProfit check may still pass
recommendation: Add slippage limit parameters to ExecuteParams for each swap step. Extend the pumpPriceLimit/unwindPriceLimit pattern to all swaps.
